study: resizing the #176 packet from 30 chains to 20 -- feasibility
reason: annotator time. Not motivated by any verdict observed: the three judged chains are 1 faithful and 2 inferred_but_reasonable, zero unsupported, so nothing seen so far bears on the rate the study reports.

what_survives.note: Unchanged at 1.0. Coverage is what licenses post-stratification, and it depends on which strata are occupied rather than on n.
what_survives.heaviest_stratum_untouched: faithful_both_agree carries 37.8% of the population weight and the packet only ever held 4 chains in it. All 4 survive, so the dominant variance term is identical at 30 and at 20 -- which is why the interval barely moves.

zero_count_ceiling.explanation: P1 predicts `unsupported` stays rare. If it is zero the study's sharpest sentence is a ceiling, and the ceiling is set by n alone. This is the largest single cost of the cut.

reviewer_comments_unaffected.R9: a human validates something -- answered by any defensible sample
reviewer_comments_unaffected.R12: source spans -- the rubric captures risk_quote and intervention_quote
reviewer_comments_unaffected.R21: gates unvalidated -- arm B still gives a direction, as at 6
reviewer_comments_unaffected.R11: inter-annotator agreement -- already open with one annotator; 7 of 8 double-coded rows survive, so a second annotator remains possible
reviewer_comments_unaffected.R13: asked for 50-100 chain-yielding documents. 30 already failed it and 20 fails it the same way, so the defence does not change: a stratified sample with full population coverage and a post-stratified estimator beats a simple random sample of the same size.

LIMITS: The hours below rest on three measured chains (30, 60, 60 minutes) and the marginal cost of the recall enumeration is measured on exactly one document, so the range is wide on purpose. Re-check at chain 5 as the run record says.

cost_hours.basis: verdict-only 45 min (mean of C01 30 and C02 60); recall 60-90 min
